stem.text: The temperature of a liquid in a laboratory flask is modeled by a differentiable function H of time t, measured in minutes, whose rate of change is \( H'(t) = 7 e^{- \frac{t}{10}} \) degrees Celsius per minute, for \( 0 \le t \le 30 \). Using a calculator, find \( H'(7) \), showing the setup, and interpret the value in the context of the problem with correct units. Give the value correct to three decimal places.

answer_key.label: \( H'(7) = 3.476 \), so at time t = 7 minutes the temperature of the liquid is increasing at a rate of 3.476 degrees Celsius per minute.

worked_solution.text: With a calculator, \( H'(7) = 3.476 \) to three decimal places.
worked_solution.rule_named: evaluate the derivative at the instant

worked_solution.text: The value is positive, so at time t = 7 minutes the temperature of the liquid is increasing at a rate of 3.476 degrees Celsius per minute.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the rate gives the direction of change

options.derivation: the independent variable never named, so the input is read as a value of the quantity rather than a time
